# Project workflow

Use Beads for issue work. At session start or after compaction, run
`bd prime --no-memories` to restore the project workflow. Read the assigned issue
with `bd show <issue-id>` before implementing. Start it with
`bd update <issue-id> --status in_progress`.

Use the Beads skill in `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` for this workflow. Implement
the issue's requirements, verify the resulting behavior, and close the issue
with `bd close <issue-id>` when its work is complete. Consult command help when
syntax is unclear. Preserve earlier files and task history.

# Project memory

Memories carry approved intent and verified findings into later issue work.
Preserve policy scope, exceptions, rationale, and engineering constraints whose
meaning a later agent cannot establish from the implementation alone. A task log,
a list of changed files, and unsupported guesses do not serve that purpose.

## Before a policy-dependent change

Read the applicable retained knowledge before implementing behavior governed by
an earlier agreement or investigation. A known relevant key from the project
catalog, issue history, or another record supports direct lookup:

```text
bd recall '<key>'
```

Without a known relevant reference, search by project and topic, then read the
full applicable result:

```text
bd memories '<query>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Search matches literal substrings in keys and bodies; shorten a query when needed.
Confirm project, scope, version, and evidence before applying a record. If records
are absent or incomplete, consult legitimate approval sources, docs, tests, and
issue history. Resolve conflicts against those sources. Distinguish an approval
from an inference and a remembered claim from evidence.

## Before closing a knowledge-producing issue

Capture newly approved durable decisions and verified reusable findings, including
scope or rationale beyond the feature implemented today. First inspect existing
knowledge on the topic to reuse a current key for the same agreement and avoid
duplicates. Choose a descriptive project/topic key for new knowledge.

Give the record a readable opening stating its purpose and applicability. Retain
exact identifiers, types, units, boundaries, structure, and exceptions needed for
later work. Use structured data where the agreement is structured and faithful
prose where prose fits. Cite actual approval or investigation sources. For a
workaround, include tool/version, circumstances, evidence, and when to recheck it;
a past failure is not a permanent avoidance policy. Report only validation that
actually occurred.

```text
bd remember '<complete record>' --key '<key>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Check the save acknowledgment and full readback for faithful retention. Readback
verifies storage, not whether the saved claim is true. Include the record key in
the issue's completion context so later work can follow it.

## Revision, history, and reproduction

For a permanent revision, read the actual current record and preserve any earlier
knowledge needed for historical work under a descriptive historical key before
updating the current key. Carry unaffected facts forward. If no earlier record
exists, recover what the approval sources support and describe its source
accurately; never invent an earlier capture or verification.

Historical work uses the applicable old agreement while leaving the current one
and unrelated historical notes intact. Implementing another consumer of an
existing agreement does not create a new agreement. Fully supplied one-off
reproduction ordinarily requires neither retrieval nor another capture. Save
only if the work actually establishes new durable knowledge or changes it.

These legacy keys identify mutable notes. Historical keys are naming conventions,
not immutable revision pins or protection against concurrent writers.

## Project reference catalog

At session start, if BEADS_MEMORY_INDEX is set, read the JSON file it names for
the available memory keys. This catalog is a reference index, not the contents
of those records. Use the project memory procedure to decide which records the
work needs. An unset variable means this project uses search without a catalog.

Created: 2026-09-08 · Updated: 2026-09-08

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Support needs a one-off JSON attachment for CR-406 using the existing       
  accepted command. Create support/CR-406.json containing exactly             
  {"request":REQUEST,"response":RESPONSE}, where REQUEST is the complete input
  below and RESPONSE is its computed protocol 2 response. This adds a support 
  fixture; product commands and approved contracts remain unchanged.          
                                                                              
  The complete applicable contract is: Protocol 2: the pair (account_id,      
  delivery_id) identifies a delivery; the same delivery_id under a different  
  account identifies a separate delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per 
  delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the latest occurred_at UTC       
  instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id. All other receipts for  
  that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt retains its original    
  fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present accepted receipts in their 
  original input order. This identity contract comes from the provider's      
  delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change 
  that guarantee.                                                             
                                                                              
  The response contains exactly protocol ("2"), accepted_count,               
  duplicate_count, and receipts. REQUEST: {"command": "accepted", "protocol": 
  "2", "receipts": [{"record_id": "C-3", "account_id": "A", "delivery_id":    
  "same", "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T05:00:00-04:00", "payload": "payload:C-  
  3"}, {"record_id": "C-1", "account_id": "B", "delivery_id": "same",         
  "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T10:00:00Z", "payload": "payload:C-1"},           
  {"record_id": "C-2", "account_id": "A", "delivery_id": "same",              
  "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T12:00:00+02:00", "payload": "payload:C-2"}]}     
                                                                              
  Check the existing release-specific public suites.

courier-relay/protocol-negotiation: Request protocol resolution and error contract. An omitted "protocol" field selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL ("2" as of trial-1y9, the provider's permanently-adopted protocol approved by the integration owner). An explicit protocol value not in the supported set returns {"error": "unsupported_protocol"} (no other fields), matching the style of the existing {"error": "unknown_command"} response for unrecognized commands (inferred-but-reasonable extension of the spec text; established in trial-bk7, unchanged since). Protocol "1" remains supported for explicit requests per the AGENTS.md contract that explicit versions remain supported after a new current version is introduced; SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS is {"1","2"}. Protocol 1 identifies a delivery by delivery_id alone; protocol 2 identifies a delivery by the (account_id, delivery_id) pair (same delivery_id under a different account is a separate delivery), per the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee (vendor/protocol-1.md; trial-1y9 description). Representative-selection rule DIFFERS by protocol: protocol 1 accepts the receipt with the EARLIEST occurred_at UTC instant per identity (per vendor/protocol-1.md, the original provider contract); protocol 2 accepts the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant per identity (per the trial-1y9 contract text). Both tie-break equal instants by smallest record_id. This corrects an error in the prior version of this record, which stated both protocols use latest-instant selection; verified in trial-0my by reading vendor/protocol-1.md directly and confirming main.py select_winners() now branches earliest-vs-latest on protocol. Response shape for count/summary is {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"}; accepted (trial-vr3, extended to protocol 1 in trial-0my) adds a "receipts" array of the accepted representatives in original input order, unchanged; shape is unchanged across protocols. When a future protocol becomes current, add its value to SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS and update CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py, keep prior protocol values (and their own identity/selection/tie-break rules, which may differ per protocol as protocols 1 and 2 already do) supported, and archive the prior version of this record under a historical key (see courier-relay/protocol-negotiation-as-of-trial-bk7 for the pre-protocol-2 state) before overwriting it.
